name_en: Kaki Mochi — dried, thin-sliced rice crackers
summary_ja: 里芋やごま、のりを混ぜたもち米を蒸してつき、薄く切って陰干しした保存菓子。旧暦の正月に餅と一緒についたのが始まりとされ、低温の油でからりと揚げたり、炭火で焼いたりして食べる。
summary_en: Glutinous rice pounded with taro, sesame, and nori is sliced thin and air-dried into a keeping snack — said to trace to pounding it alongside New Year's mochi, later fried in low-temperature oil or toasted over charcoal.
source_title: かき餅 千葉県 | うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

name_en: Juubako-iri Botamochi — layered rice-cake sweet for a newborn's third day
summary_ja: もち米ご飯とあんこを一つひとつ丸めず重箱に敷き詰め、好きな分だけ取り分けて食べるぼたもち。子どもが生まれて三日目に配る祝いの風習で食べられ、産後の母親に栄養をという願いが込められていると伝わる。
summary_en: Sweet rice and red-bean paste are layered whole into a lacquered box rather than shaped into individual mounds, so each person takes as much as they like — made to mark a baby's third day, a custom said to carry the hope of nourishing a mother soon after birth.
source_title: 重箱入りぼたもち／おはぎ 千葉県 | うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

name_en: Tenmondou — root vegetables candied in sugar syrup
summary_ja: ごぼうやれんこん、しょうがなど繊維の多い野菜を薄く切ってゆで、砂糖でじっくり煮詰めて乾燥させた保存菓子。漢方薬の天門冬を蜜漬けにした昔の薬用の食べ方が名の由来とされ、農繁期のおやつとして食べられてきた。
summary_en: Fibrous vegetables like burdock, lotus root, and ginger are boiled thin, then slow-simmered in sugar and dried into a keeping sweet — its name is said to trace to an old herbal remedy of asparagus root steeped in honey, and it was eaten as a snack to fuel farm work during the busy season.
source_title: てんもんどう 千葉県 | うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

name_en: Barappa Manju — steamed bun wrapped in catbrier leaf
summary_ja: 収穫したばかりの小麦を挽いた生地にあんを包み、サルトリイバラ（ばらっぱ）の葉を下に敷いて蒸す北総地域の饅頭。夏祭りやお盆に人が集まると材料を持ち寄ってつくられてきたと伝わる。
summary_en: Freshly milled wheat dough is wrapped around red bean paste and steamed on a leaf of catbrier, called barappa locally — a bun said to be made in Chiba's Hokuso area when people gathered for summer festivals or Obon, each bringing ingredients to share.
source_title: ばらっぱまんじゅう 千葉県 | うちの郷土料理：農林水産省
